environment: disposable PostgreSQL 16 database and least-privilege app role in isolated local qa005-postgres container; fresh QA-only CP/DP and Master KEK under /tmp/qa005-cp45; Chromium; synthetic Owner. No Valkey configured for this run; existing container was standalone, not a cluster.

steps: Provision an isolated PostgreSQL database and app role.
Start exact-source control-plane role and complete fresh setup in Chromium.
Start a separate exact-source data-plane process against the same PostgreSQL database and Master KEK.
Verify both /readyz listeners, send unauthenticated GET /v1/models to the Data Plane, and inspect authenticated cluster-status API and Operations UI.
healthy_split_role_reproduction.visual_ui: Cluster nodes 2; both node IDs, roles, config epoch 1, heartbeat age, and OK state displayed.

steps: Terminate only the disposable Data Plane process.
Wait for it to stop responding and 12 seconds for heartbeat expiry.
Refresh Operations > Health & Cluster and read cluster-status again.
node_loss_followup.visual_ui: Ready; Cluster nodes 1; sole control-plane row reports OK. The departed Data Plane is removed and no incomplete/unreachable/expected-count indicator is shown.

historical_reconciliation: The original RC6 failure (ready split Data Plane entirely absent while runtime was operating) did not reproduce on this fresh RC7 healthy two-process path. A node-loss follow-up shows the inventory removes the vanished Data Plane after heartbeat expiry and reports a ready single-node view. Because this setup had no expected replica count/topology input, whether that UI behavior violates the active-node versus unreachable-node operational contract is unresolved. Fresh status is PARTIAL, not a clean pass.
visual_inspection: The healthy two-node inventory and post-termination one-node view were visually inspected.
